canonical_name: Peano existence theorem for ordinary differential equations
source_claim_verbatim_translation: Existence of solutions under a continuity condition.
canonical_statement: Provisional classical scope: for an initial-value problem x'(t) = f(t, x(t)), x(t0) = x0 in a finite-dimensional real state space, continuity of f on a suitable neighborhood of (t0, x0) implies existence of at least one local solution through (t0, x0). The exact neighborhood, interval, regularity, and endpoint formulation must be frozen from a selected source theorem in the statement phase.
domain_and_universes: Candidate domain is time in Real and state in a finite-dimensional real normed space (classically Real^n). The exact dimension encoding, norm, neighborhood, interval, and Lean universes remain open.
ordered_binders: candidate finite-dimensional real state space E
candidate initial time t0 : Real and initial state x0 : E
candidate vector field f : Real -> E -> E
candidate neighborhood parameters and local interval
hypotheses: f is continuous on an explicitly selected neighborhood of (t0, x0)
the selected neighborhood supplies the local boundedness/compactness data used to choose a nontrivial time interval
any positivity, closed-rectangle, dimensional, or endpoint assumptions required by the selected source are explicit
conclusion: There exist a nontrivial interval containing t0 and a differentiable curve x on it such that x(t0) = x0 and x'(t) = f(t, x(t)) throughout the interval, with the precise derivative-at-endpoints encoding still open.
statement_choices_requiring_source_audit: open-neighborhood formulation versus a closed time-state rectangle
unspecified local interval versus the quantitative h = min(a, b/M) interval
classical derivative at interior points versus derivative-within at endpoints
continuous solution satisfying an integral equation versus a differentiable ODE solution

alternate_encodings.target: a curve satisfying x(t) = x0 + integral from t0 to t of f(s, x(s)) ds
alternate_encodings.relationship: candidate equivalence to the differential formulation under the selected continuity and interval hypotheses

alternate_encodings.target: existence on |t - t0| <= min(a, b/M) when f is continuous and norm-bounded by M on the corresponding rectangle

excluded_degenerate_cases: No boundary convention is frozen at intake. In particular a zero-width time interval cannot witness local existence; M = 0, zero-dimensional state, one-sided domains, boundary initial points, and non-Lipschitz examples with nonunique solutions must be explicit statement-phase probes.
excluded_neighboring_claims: Picard-Lindelof existence and uniqueness under a Lipschitz condition
uniqueness, continuous dependence, stability, or numerical convergence
foundation_profile: Open rev-5.6 profile: the classical proof normally uses compactness/equicontinuity and may require choice; all logical, topological, and integration dependencies require audit.
tcb_profile: Lean 4 kernel plus the repository-pinned mathlib; exact imports and transitive dependency fingerprints are deferred to the statement phase.
computation_profile: No numerical ODE solver, approximation experiment, native computation, oracle, or external theorem is credited at intake.
source_revisions: Discovery anchors and their limitations are recorded in source_statement_crosswalk.md. No immutable primary-source receipt, exact theorem/page transcription, translation audit, or errata review has been accepted.

PEANO-BOUND local bound and positive interval selection
